Summary Diagnostics Explanations Per-Function Details

Rust vs C: Block Matching Accuracy Across Optimization Levels

Experiment: 100 functions × 2 languages = 200 function pairs. Each function pair is analyzed at O0 vs O2 using 4 independent block-matching methods.

Features tested: Ownership & Move, Drop Glue (RAII), Bounds Checking, ? Operator (Option/Result), Panic/Unwind Paths — 20 functions each.

Methods: Value-based (concrete execution outputs), Opcodes (opcode set Jaccard), Constants (constant set Jaccard), Size (instruction count ratio).

Question: Which language's functions are easier to match across optimization levels, and WHY does each Rust-specific feature help or hurt matching accuracy?

Diagnostic Analysis: Why Value-Based Matching Is Low

Root Cause: Why Value-Based Matching Scores Are Low

Value-based matching (concrete micro-execution outputs) shows Rust 25–31% vs C 25–47% accuracy. Three compounding problems explain this:

Problem 1: Register Allocation Diverges

O0 uses arg0-arg3 + ret0 (5 registers). O2 uses up to 13 registers including callee-saved (saved0-4, r10) that don't exist in O0.

concrete_value_similarity() only compares common registers. When O2 spills key computations into registers O0 never uses, there's nothing to compare.

Empirically: only ~5–8% of (register, value) pairs overlap between O0 and O2 blocks.

Problem 2: 44% of Matched Pairs Lack Comparable Outputs

Both Have OutputsOne Side OnlyNeither
Rust 1427 (56%) 556 543
C 868 (69%) 214 177

Prologue, bounds-check-only, and call-only blocks produce no concrete outputs. Rust has more such blocks (31% BODY blocks lack outputs vs 18% in C).

Problem 3: Even Comparable Pairs Show Low Overlap

Among pairs where both blocks have concrete outputs:

Mean SimAbove 0.3 Threshold
Rust 0.353 50%
C 0.346 53%

O2 restructures computations (constant folding, loop invariant hoisting, operation merging), so even blocks computing the “same thing” produce different intermediate register values.

Overall Similarity Distribution

MeanMedian>0.3In [0.15, 0.30]
Rust 0.3060.250 29%71%
C 0.3150.250 38%61%

Median sim = 0.25 means the 50%-weighted value component contributes ~0. The 0.25 comes entirely from dataflow (25%) + memory (15%) + constants (10%).

Block Count: Rust vs C

Avg O0 BlocksAvg O2 BlocksRatio
Rust 3629 1.26x
C 1414 1.01x

Rust has 2.5× more blocks on average. More blocks = more pairwise comparisons = more noise in Hungarian matching = lower accuracy. O2 also eliminates/merges Rust safety blocks, creating large O0:O2 block count mismatches (up to 12:1).

Why C Wins on Value-Based but Rust Wins on Size

Value-based (C wins): C functions have fewer, simpler blocks (avg 14 vs 36). With fewer blocks, Hungarian matching has less noise. C's straightforward register usage means more output overlap survives O2 optimization.

Size (Rust wins): Rust's extra safety blocks (bounds checks, drop glue, panic paths) are small, fixed-pattern blocks whose instruction counts barely change between O0 and O2. They act as “anchors” for size-based matching. C lacks these anchors, and its core computation blocks change size more dramatically under O2.

Per-Feature Explanations

Ownership & Move

Value-based

Rust: 29% (192/659)  |  C: 34% (100/294)

C wins (C: 29% vs Rust: 34%). C's simple pointer copies yield minimal block structure that survives optimization unchanged. Rust's ownership transfer blocks get reorganized by O2. Value-based matching shows C blocks produce more consistent concrete outputs across O-levels.

Opcodes

Rust: 58% (383/659)  |  C: 83% (243/294)

C wins (C: 58% vs Rust: 83%). C's simple pointer copies yield minimal block structure that survives optimization unchanged. Rust's ownership transfer blocks get reorganized by O2. Opcode sets in C blocks are more stable across optimization.

Constants

Rust: 1% (7/659)  |  C: 12% (35/294)

C wins (C: 1% vs Rust: 12%). C's simple pointer copies yield minimal block structure that survives optimization unchanged. Rust's ownership transfer blocks get reorganized by O2. C's constant immediates are better preserved at O2.

Size

Rust: 78% (513/659)  |  C: 77% (226/294)

TIE: Both languages show similar block matching accuracy.

Drop Glue (RAII)

Value-based

Rust: 31% (219/717)  |  C: 40% (140/347)

C wins (C: 31% vs Rust: 40%). C's manual free() calls are simple and predictable across O-levels. Rust's drop glue blocks get inlined or eliminated at O2. Value-based matching shows C blocks produce more consistent concrete outputs across O-levels.

Opcodes

Rust: 58% (417/717)  |  C: 81% (281/347)

C wins (C: 58% vs Rust: 81%). C's manual free() calls are simple and predictable across O-levels. Rust's drop glue blocks get inlined or eliminated at O2. Opcode sets in C blocks are more stable across optimization.

Constants

Rust: 2% (17/717)  |  C: 17% (58/347)

C wins (C: 2% vs Rust: 17%). C's manual free() calls are simple and predictable across O-levels. Rust's drop glue blocks get inlined or eliminated at O2. C's constant immediates are better preserved at O2.

Size

Rust: 86% (613/717)  |  C: 75% (259/347)

Rust wins (Rust: 85% vs C: 75%). Rust's drop_in_place calls create distinctive block signatures (callee + cleanup pattern) that survive O2. C's manual free() is indistinguishable from other function calls. Rust's block instruction counts change less between O0 and O2.

Bounds Checking

Value-based

Rust: 25% (107/426)  |  C: 25% (56/225)

TIE: Both languages show similar block matching accuracy.

Opcodes

Rust: 74% (314/426)  |  C: 79% (177/225)

C wins (C: 74% vs Rust: 79%). Without bounds checks, C functions have fewer blocks and simpler CFGs. Optimization preserves the core computation blocks. Rust's bounds check blocks are eliminated/merged at O2, disrupting alignment. Opcode sets in C blocks are more stable across optimization.

Constants

Rust: 2% (8/426)  |  C: 8% (17/225)

C wins (C: 2% vs Rust: 8%). Without bounds checks, C functions have fewer blocks and simpler CFGs. Optimization preserves the core computation blocks. Rust's bounds check blocks are eliminated/merged at O2, disrupting alignment. C's constant immediates are better preserved at O2.

Size

Rust: 88% (375/426)  |  C: 69% (155/225)

Rust wins (Rust: 88% vs C: 69%). Rust's bounds check blocks (cmp+jae+ud2) have distinctive patterns that persist even under O2 (cannot be fully eliminated without unsafe). C has no bounds checks, fewer blocks to match. Rust's block instruction counts change less between O0 and O2.

? Operator (Option/Result)

Value-based

Rust: 29% (102/355)  |  C: 46% (102/224)

C wins (C: 29% vs Rust: 46%). C's return-code checking is straightforward cmp+branch that optimizes predictably. Rust's ? operator blocks undergo layout changes at O2. Value-based matching shows C blocks produce more consistent concrete outputs across O-levels.

Opcodes

Rust: 59% (209/355)  |  C: 73% (164/224)

C wins (C: 59% vs Rust: 73%). C's return-code checking is straightforward cmp+branch that optimizes predictably. Rust's ? operator blocks undergo layout changes at O2. Opcode sets in C blocks are more stable across optimization.

Constants

Rust: 3% (9/355)  |  C: 12% (28/224)

C wins (C: 3% vs Rust: 12%). C's return-code checking is straightforward cmp+branch that optimizes predictably. Rust's ? operator blocks undergo layout changes at O2. C's constant immediates are better preserved at O2.

Size

Rust: 93% (330/355)  |  C: 80% (180/224)

Rust wins (Rust: 93% vs C: 80%). The ? operator generates discriminant-check+branch blocks with consistent patterns (test discriminant → extract payload → propagate error). These survive O2 because the error path must remain. Rust's block instruction counts change less between O0 and O2.

Panic/Unwind Paths

Value-based

Rust: 27% (101/369)  |  C: 47% (80/169)

C wins (C: 27% vs Rust: 47%). C's error handling is inline (return -1) with no special cold paths. Simpler structure survives optimization better than Rust's panic machinery. Value-based matching shows C blocks produce more consistent concrete outputs across O-levels.

Opcodes

Rust: 51% (188/369)  |  C: 73% (124/169)

C wins (C: 51% vs Rust: 73%). C's error handling is inline (return -1) with no special cold paths. Simpler structure survives optimization better than Rust's panic machinery. Opcode sets in C blocks are more stable across optimization.

Constants

Rust: 3% (10/369)  |  C: 18% (30/169)

C wins (C: 3% vs Rust: 18%). C's error handling is inline (return -1) with no special cold paths. Simpler structure survives optimization better than Rust's panic machinery. C's constant immediates are better preserved at O2.

Size

Rust: 88% (323/369)  |  C: 67% (114/169)

Rust wins (Rust: 88% vs C: 67%). Panic paths generate cold blocks with distinctive callee signatures (core::panicking::*) that are easily matched. These paths are preserved even at O2 because they cannot be proven unreachable. Rust's block instruction counts change less between O0 and O2.
